### Observed differences

- A01 became more frequent and more often repeated: trace participation rose from about 28% to 53%, and mean occurrences per trace from 0.53 to 1.10. [OCC001]
- A07 became less frequent and less often repeated: trace participation fell from about 51% to 29%, and mean occurrences per trace from 1.03 to 0.57. [OCC002]
- The main successor of A01 changed from A07 (about 94% of outgoing transitions) to A05 (about 57%) and A06 (about 18%); A07 is no longer a successor of A01. [DIR001]
- The main successor of A05 changed from A01 (about 96%) to A07 (about 91%). [DIR004]
- The main successor of A07 changed from A05/A06 (about 43%/41%) to A01 (about 94%). [DIR006]
- A03 and A04 now often lead to A01 instead of A07: A03→A01 rose from about 1% to 34%, A04→A01 from about 3% to 39%, while A03→A07 fell from about 51% to 2% and A04→A07 from about 41% to 1%. [DIR002, DIR003]
- A06 moved from near the end of traces (mean position 0.96) to the middle (mean position 0.48), and its direct successor profile broadened from only A03/A04 to include A01, A05 and A07. [POS003, DIR005]
- A07 now always appears together with A05 (previously A07 could appear alone in about 23% of traces), and A07 also always appears with A01, A03, A04 and A06 when present. [REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- Lag distances changed accordingly: A01 and A05 became closer (lag 1 instead of lag 2), A01 and A06 became closer (lag 1 instead of lag 2), while A01 and A07 became further apart (lag 2 instead of lag 1). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in the ordering of activities in the main loop: the sequence A01 → A07 → A05 → A01 appears to have been replaced by A01 → A05 → A07 → A01, with A06 as an alternative to A05 after A01. This is directly shown by the successor shifts (A01 no longer leads to A07, A05 now leads to A07, A07 now leads to A01) and by the lag changes (A01–A05 and A01–A06 become closer, A01–A07 becomes more distant). A03 and A04 now feed into A01 instead of A07, consistent with the same reordering. The large number of qualifying items (35 vs. 0.29 expected by chance) makes a chance explanation unlikely.

Other differences: A01 increased in participation and repetition, while A07 decreased, which may reflect a shift in how often the loop is entered or repeated, but this is secondary to the ordering change. A limitation is that A06's outgoing transitions before the change are based on only 11 observations, so some details of A06's role are less certain.
